target.canonical_statement: Does every set of n distinct points in R^2 determine >> n/sqrt(log n) many distinct distances?

verdict_detail: The conjecture is neither proved nor disproved by this campaign. Banked: a sorry-free elementary Omega(sqrt n) lower bound (rung 1) and a sorry-free gap ledger proving rung 1 is asymptotically negligible against the target.

cannot_be_closed_by_search.reason: the statement quantifies over ALL n-point subsets of R^2 for ALL large n with a uniform constant; no finite configuration search is evidence about it
cannot_be_closed_by_search.source: erdosproblems.com/89 states the problem cannot be resolved with a finite computation
cannot_be_closed_by_search.consequence: NO point-configuration search was run as evidence in this campaign

literature_position.status: elementary; THIS is what is formalized here
shows the conjecture is best possible

prior_art.verdict: KNOWN_OPEN_PROBLEM; no paper in the corpus improves on n/log n in the plane

near_misses_ruled_off_target.title: Solution to a Problem of Erdos Concerning Distances and Points
near_misses_ruled_off_target.author: Benjamin Grayzel
near_misses_ruled_off_target.why_off_target: solves a DIFFERENT 1997 Erdos question: an n-point set with O(n/sqrt log n) distinct distances subject to every 4-point subset determining at least 3 distances; built from the lattice {(x, sqrt2*y)} with Bernays' theorem on u^2+2v^2. It is a construction on the upper-bound side of a constrained variant and says nothing about problem 89's lower bound.

near_misses_ruled_off_target.title: Remarks on the disproof of the unit distance conjecture
near_misses_ruled_off_target.why_off_target: unit distances is a different Erdos problem; the distinct-distances lower bound is untouched

statement_firewall.checked: minimalDistinctDistances returns Nat but its set-builder body is cast to R
statement_firewall.elaborated_form: fun n => sInf {x : Nat | exists points, exists (_ : #points = n), (distinctDistances points : R) = (x : R)}
statement_firewall.why_inert: Nat.cast injectivity; it is a Nat.sInf over a Set Nat

banked_results.headline: sqrt_isBigO_minimalDistinctDistances : (fun n => Real.sqrt n) =O[atTop] (fun n => (minimalDistinctDistances n : R))
banked_results.proof_idea: Erdos 1946 pigeonhole: fix p != q; x |-> (dist x p, dist x q) maps P\{p,q} into D x D and every fibre has at most 2 elements (two circles with distinct centres meet twice), so #P - 2 <= 2|D|^2.

banked_results.headline: sqrt_isLittleO_target : (fun n => Real.sqrt n) =o[atTop] (fun n => n / Real.sqrt (Real.log n))
banked_results.purpose: rung 1 is STRICTLY and asymptotically negligibly below the target; target_implies_rung1 shows rung 1 is a NECESSARY CONSEQUENCE of the conjecture, i.e. consistency and not evidence

grid_measurement.label: CONSTRUCTION MEASUREMENT, NOT EVIDENCE for the lower bound
grid_measurement.arithmetic: exact integers for the count (distinct values of a^2+b^2); floats only in the benchmark ratios
grid_measurement.finding: D(grid) / (n/sqrt(log n)) is FLAT at ~1.11 across k=20..120 (a 36x range of n), while D/(n/log n) grows 2.68 -> 3.43 and D/sqrt(n) grows 8.95 -> 42.98
grid_measurement.interpretation: the grid tracks n/sqrt(log n) (the conjectured order), sits a growing factor ABOVE n/log n (Guth-Katz has room), and runs away from sqrt n (rung 1 is nowhere near). Consistent with n/sqrt(log n) being the right order; NOT evidence for the lower bound.

explicitly_not_proved: All three sorry's in the upstream 89.lean remain sorry; this campaign did not touch that file.

next_rung_ordered_by_cost.note: already-solved mathematics, still sorry upstream. Single missing primitive: the << half of Landau-Ramanujan, #{m <= N : m = a^2+b^2} << N/sqrt(log N). Not in Mathlib. HIGHEST-VALUE REACHABLE TARGET; it is a number-theory job, not a geometry one.
